ledger.x: 1788: Pōmare I becomes the first king of unified Tahiti.
1808: rebels drive Pōmare II from Tahiti to Moʻorea.
1815: Pōmare II wins Tahiti back at Te Feipī.

ledger.cpn: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)
Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)

ledger.x: 1880: Pōmare V gives Tahiti and its dependencies to France.

wars.name: Franco-Tahitian War
wars.outcome: French victory: Fort Fautaua fell on 17 December 1846 and Queen Pōmare IV returned from exile in February 1847 to rule under the protectorate; the Anglo-French Convention of 1847 recognised the independence of Huahine, Raiatea and Bora Bora.

wars.name: Tahitian civil war and Battle of Te Feipī
wars.outcome: Pōmare II, who had taken refuge in Moʻorea on 22 December 1808, won the decisive Battle of Te Feipī on 12 November 1815 and was baptised on 16 May 1819.

certainty.note: Island coasts are exact; what is soft is the extent of Pōmare authority (Tetiʻaroa, Mehetiʻa, the Tuamotus, the nominal suzerainty over the Leeward Islands).
Protectorate of France; the islands are the same, the Leeward kingdoms stay outside until 1888-1897.
